pages.notes: This is a declassified FBI folder cover with extensive red routing stamps and handling marks; the OCR completely garbled the content, missing 'INVESTIGATION', 'DO NOT DESTROY', 'Transfer-Call 421', FOIA routing information, and multiple dated stamps visible on the folder.
1947 FBI memo with aged paper, multiple red handwritten annotations, and office stamps; OCR captured main body text well but garbled header area ("OVERNMEN" for GOVERNMENT, "-#trmNG" for FLYING).

OCR captured document structure but contains multiple word-level errors: 'HEADQUA' (missing 'RTERS FOURTH AIR'), 'Plying' (Flying), 'ant Chief of Steff' (Assistant Chief of Staff), 'atellicence' (A-2 Intelligence), 'similerity' (similarity), 'mattere' (matter), and missed the date '25 August 1947' entirely in header.

Typewritten letter with handwritten redactions/signature; OCR severely fragmented the coherent text into disconnected fragments, though scan itself is readable with visible aging and bleed-through artifacts.

Document is a Standard Form 64 memo with clear OCR errors: 'STANRARD' (should be STANDARD), 'FLYING DIGS' (should be FLYING DISCS - critical error), and possible date error (1937 vs 1947 given August 27, 1947 reference in body). Body text and routing marks captured well despite age staining and handwritten annotations.

Military memo with clear typewritten text; OCR struggles with character substitutions (e.g., 'Assistant' → 'Assistent', 'A-2' → 'Aq2', 'Building' → '8uilding') and phantom header text ('se cCecpDer'), but core intelligence report content about Guam sightings is captured despite numerous errors.
Largely blank page with red handwritten reference number (62-8394-102) at top and ENCLOSURE stamp; OCR failed to capture the visible handwritten annotation.

Clear typewritten memo with multiple OCR errors: 'Steff' for Staff, 'A~2' for A-2, 'informations' for information, 'Lte' for Lt., '¢S¢' for OSC, 'FRANCISCC' for FRANCISCO. Main content readable but corrections needed.

Standard Air Force memo from 1947 with multiple OCR errors: misread 'HEADQUARTERS FOURTH' as 'fH', 'Hamilton' as 'lamilton', 'TO:' as '70:', 'Investigation' as 'Investigetion', and abbreviated 'A-2' as 'Au2'; document warping and redaction marks at top affected character recognition.

Aged military report with CONFIDENTIAL stamps; OCR captures most content but has numerous character-level errors throughout (e.g., 'C400' for '0400', 'WE SERVICE' for 'AIR RESCUE SERVICE', 'wae'/'jumed'/'thet' for 'was'/'assumed'/'that').

Military aircraft crash incident report with systematic OCR character recognition errors; most text captured but numerous substitutions throughout (e.g., 'thet'→'that', 'orew'→'crew', 'TILE'→'WASHINGTON', 'Sgts Be Le'→'Sgt's B. L.'), degrading readability.

Typewritten military report with CONFIDENTIAL markings; OCR captures structure and most content but has systematic character-level errors (0→O substitutions, word fragments like 'B0enes'→BARNES, 'sgeret'→secret, 'Offleer'→Officer) typical of aged photocopy scanning.

The OCR captured heavily distorted fragments from the comments section (e.g., 'Cooperation recsived from' → 'Cooperation received from', 'scendies soncerned' → 'agencies concerned', 'oRraphs' → 'Photographs') while missing most structured content like section headers, statistics, and the signature block.

Typewritten military form with substantial OCR character substitution errors (H→HR, Y→Y, numbers/letters confused: '31'→'Sl', 'Mr.'→'Ure'/'Lie', 'th'/'nd' ligatures misread); text structure captured but accuracy compromised by light scan and character-level failures.

Typewritten government report form scanned at good quality; OCR exhibits frequent character-level substitution errors (l/1 confusion, consonant misreads, etc.) making text approximately 50% accurately recognized but ~85% of visible content captured in some form.

Typewritten declassified report with systematic character substitution errors throughout (e.g., 'approximately' → 'Gpproxinately', '@ige' for porthole references, 'Yeury Ialend' for Maury Island, 'enulysis' for analysis), suggesting OCR struggled with typewriter font or faded character spacing despite good scan readability.

Typewritten government form with good scan clarity but poor OCR quality; systematic character substitutions and transpositions throughout (e.g., 'check'→'cheek', 'Crisman'→'Crigwnn', 'FBI'→'FRI', 'commission'→'scumiesion') suggest typewriter font recognition issues.

Typewritten letter from R.A. Palmer to Kenneth Arnold dated July 22, 1947; OCR captures ~92% but contains multiple errors including 'pio' for 'pic', 'erticle' for 'article', 'Murry' for 'Maury', 'propsesition' for 'proposition', and 'trath' for 'truth', plus dropped articles ('611' for 'all'); CONFIDENTIAL stamps visible top/bottom.

Western Union telegram with legible typewritten text; OCR correctly captured the body content and addresses despite dark scan and margin repetition; minor formatting inconsistencies in rendered OCR output.
Page shows photograph of material/object sample cross-section with CONFIDENTIAL stamps; OCR failed to capture any text despite visible classification markings.
Nearly blank page with only faded handwritten notation at top and faint official photograph stamp from U.S. Army Air Force Hamilton Field; OCR correctly captured no substantive text.
Page contains a photograph of a physical artifact/object with visible 'CONFIDENTIAL' stamps and handwritten annotation, but OCR failed to capture any text despite readability.
Page is primarily a photograph of rock/debris samples with scale reference; OCR completely failed, generating nonsense text instead of the visible 'CONFIDENTIAL' markings.

Page is primarily a photograph of debris/material with CONFIDENTIAL markings (struck through) at top and bottom, plus handwritten notation. OCR output is severely garbled fragments bearing no clear correspondence to visible text elements.
Page contains photograph of two metallic/rocky object specimens with minimal text (CONFIDENTIAL stamps, handwritten markings). OCR captured no text despite visible classification markings and labels.

1947 government memo with handwritten notes and classification stamps; OCR captured main structure and content but has errors like 'eylinder' for 'cylinder', 'Yean' for 'Dean', and corrupted word boundaries in several passages.
Heavily degraded scan with faded typewritten text and multiple DECLASSIFIED/REDACTED stamps; OCR only captured the redaction exemption code (b)(7)(D) and missed the illegible body text.
Typewritten FBI document with clean scan; OCR has 2 character errors (Boston→4oston, secret→seoret) but captured all visible text including redaction notation and signature block.

Typewritten FBI memo on pink teletype paper with handwritten routing and stamps; OCR captures ~85% correctly but has errors including RECTOR→DIRECTOR misread, FRIM→FROM error, garbled 'APHRK' (possibly redacted), 'bag ay' corruption, and missing WEDNESDAY; redacted areas not handled cleanly.
Heavily redacted FBI document (pink-stamped) with 'RECEIVED' stamps overlaid at angles; OCR captured only garbled fragments from faded text visible through redaction marks.

Government memo with clear typewritten text and handwritten annotations. OCR captured most content but contains character substitution errors (e.g., 'Xirnold' for Arnold, 'Ralpb' for Ralph, '1917' for 1947) and missing words like 'FLYING' from the subject line.
Nearly blank microfilm page with faint handwritten/stamped annotations in bottom margin; OCR captured the visible marks but text is heavily degraded and difficult to verify character accuracy.
FBI typewritten document with minor OCR character errors in dates (1 misread as ), 4 as :) and one word truncation ('furnished' becomes 'ed') near page bottom; COPIES DESTROYED stamp clearly visible.

Typewritten page with certification stamps scanned cleanly. OCR captured ~95% of text but contains scattered character-level errors: 'possiblg' (possibly), 'cone' (come), 'iving' (giving), 'ragments' (fragments), 'hemselves' (themselves), 'Tacom:' (Tacoma).

FBI memo dated August 10, 1947 regarding flying disc sightings involving Crissman and Dahl in Tacoma, Washington; OCR severely garbled with numerous character substitution errors (e.g., 'Gureau' for 'Bureau', 'fashington' for 'Washington'), likely due to photocopy fading and quality degradation.

Typewritten declassified document about 1947 UAP incident and B-25 crash. OCR captures overall structure and most words, but has numerous character-level errors (missing letters like 'amilton' for Hamilton, 'horities' for Authorities), word breaks ('st. tated', 'wh hich'), and spacing issues ('$230: PoM.' for likely '2:30 P.M.'), plus one proper noun error ('Tacona' for Tacoma).

FBI investigation document with typewritten text; OCR struggles with spacing in names (CRISMAN becomes CR RISM AN) and some word formation errors, but overall content structure and most text is captured despite document age and fading.

Typewritten FBI document with mostly preserved structure but significant character-level OCR errors and word fragmentation (e.g., 'inno way' for 'in no way', dropped letters, malformed proper names), likely due to document age and ink fading on scan.

Aged typewritten government memo with fair scan quality; OCR captured most readable content but contains garbled sections (e.g., 'iM', 'MMIL §', '¢ TH', 'Yright Field'), incomplete redacted text, and character recognition errors typical of faded photocopies.

Typewritten government document with aging/fading and two archival stamps at top; OCR captures main content but has notable errors in names (PIRYERT MA, IOLD, DAVIDSON misspellings), terminology (newpaperman, Chad fragments, mem. cannon), and garbled sections in lower portion (MORRELLO interview details), reducing accuracy to ~75%.

Aged FBI document with grainy scan and multiple OCR errors including garbled words (amalyzed, alalyzed, Weabtngton), broken word boundaries (ock formations, fter consi able), and character substitutions (contactéd, Bvanston), though the overall structure and ~75% of the text content is captured.

FBI memo discussing Kenneth Arnold UFO sighting investigation; OCR has captured the general structure and content but contains numerous errors including fragmented words (e.g., 'i in:which', 'ng discs', 'thet inthrop'), missing characters, and corrupted sequences throughout that significantly impact readability.

Typewritten FBI memo on aged photocopy with visible redaction marks; OCR captured structure but has significant character recognition errors (e.g., 'duly' for 'July', 'P ALMER' for 'PALMER') and spacing issues particularly in lower-density sections.

Photocopy of typewritten government document with scattered OCR errors (e.g., 'the -C)', 'HL story', garbled word fragments) but core narrative and proper names (ARNOLD, DAHL, CRISMAN, DAVIDSON, BROWN) mostly preserved; faded areas and photocopy degradation reduced OCR confidence.

Typewritten government document with significant OCR corruption including character truncation, fragmented words, and critical errors (1917 vs 1947 in opening date); approximately half of visible text captured in recognizable form despite heavy character-level degradation.

Typewritten FBI document with substantial fading and degradation; OCR captured structure but garbled numerous words with missing/incorrect characters throughout (e.g., 'eomatlony' for information, 'SUDTE' for SUITE, 'nite as @ sheet' for white as a sheet), making about 45% of text reasonably recoverable.

Typewritten page with legible content visible to human eye, but OCR output is severely fragmented and corrupted—words are broken into fragments, sentence structure is lost, and proper nouns are mangled (e.g., 'SMITH' becomes scattered parts). The scan shows aging, dust spots, and slight fading that likely contributed to OCR failure.

Typewritten document with visible grain/noise from microfilm scanning; OCR captured ~50% of words recognizably despite significant character-level garbling (e.g., 'SMITH and ARNOLD' rendered as 'TH and LD'), likely due to fading and microfilm degradation.

Typewritten FBI memorandum from August 1947 about a UAP incident; OCR captured most words but struggles with letter recognition (missing initial capitals, character substitutions like 'oe' for 'of'), typical of aged document scans with staining and degradation.
Manila enclosure envelope with red 'ENCLOSURE' stamps and faint handwritten notations; mostly blank space with minimal text content that OCR failed to capture.

OCR severely fragmented this typed statement, capturing scattered phrases while missing most paragraph structure, proper names (Mac Culloch, FBI designation), and full sentences; handwritten signatures at bottom likely disrupted downstream text recognition.

Typewritten affidavit with slight rightward skew and minor OCR character/punctuation interpretations (e.g., '-=-' dash notation), but nearly all narrative text captured accurately—this is Kenneth Arnold's 1947 sworn account of interviewing UFO witnesses in Tacoma.

Mostly blank page with faint handwritten notations (numbers/marks) and visible center fold crease; OCR correctly returned empty since minimal printed content exists.

OCR captured only the first portion with multiple character errors (CKISMAN→CRISMAN, HAROID→HAROLD), completely missed the location 'Tacoma, Washington' and reference markings, and failed to capture 'of EMIL J.' from the title.

Page is mostly blank with only handwritten reference number at top (62-83494-107) and DECLASSIFIED stamp; OCR captured nothing despite visible handwriting.

Affidavit page with substantial typewritten body text; OCR captured only fragmented words from the middle of the document, missing context and most of the multi-paragraph statement about the July 1947 sighting.

Declassified typewritten document with visible agent notes about an unidentified object investigation, but OCR failed to capture any text despite content being legible.

Pink declassified document with heavily faded typewritten text making OCR impossible; visible stamps include 'RECEIVED TELETYPE UNIT' and date '15 7:55 PM 47'; text is too faint to capture despite structural visibility.

Typewritten FBI memo from 1947 with mostly accurate OCR, but several character misreadings: 'steted' for 'stated', multiple 'thet' for 'that', and some spacing issues in redacted sections with censored names marked as © or bracketed.

Blank file folder page with a single faint handwritten reference number (622-83694-III) in upper right corner; OCR completely failed to capture this minimal text.

Page contains clearly visible typewritten biographical text about Kenneth Arnold with a redacted section marked in red, but OCR returned no text despite readable scan quality, indicating a processing failure.

Typewritten page containing multiple readable paragraphs about Kenneth Arnold's fire control business and flying experience; OCR extracted zero text despite clear legibility, likely due to faded photocopy scan characteristics.
Page contains substantial typewritten narrative with handwritten red circle annotations, but OCR text is completely empty despite clearly readable text throughout the document.

Typewritten page with substantial visible text describing aerial observations; contains ~300+ words legible to human readers, but OCR extracted zero characters, likely due to red stamp/redaction marks overlaid on portions of the text.
Page contains clearly legible typewritten text with red circle marks overlaid (likely redactions or annotations), but OCR captured no text whatsoever despite good scan quality and readable content.

Typewritten page with multiple paragraphs of clearly readable text and a red COPY stamp, but OCR completely failed to capture any characters despite good scan quality and legible typeface.

Mixed handwritten and typewritten July 1947 letter to Raymond A. Palmer signed by Kenneth Arnold with handwritten annotations; OCR completely failed to extract visible typewritten body text or handwritten content despite legible content.

Cover page with received/teletype routing stamps (AUG 14, 1947) and FBI markings, but document is heavily faded making nearly all text illegible for OCR.

Heavily faded typewritten document with redaction stamps and aging damage; text is barely legible even to human inspection, explaining why OCR produced zero characters.
